chunks: And with this chain, from al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever recites 'Iqra bi-smi rabbik' (Recite in the name of your Lord) during his day or night, and then dies on that day or night, he dies as a martyr, and Allah raises him as a martyr and gives him life as a martyr, and he is like the one who struck with his sword in the cause of Allah alongside the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ: Recite in the name of your Lord (opening of Surah Alaq)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Alaq and dying on the same day?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to emphasize the spiritual potency of the first revelation, linking the act of recitation directly to the highest status of martyrdom (shahada). In Shia tradition, this equivalence underscores that the intellectual and spiritual struggle of internalizing the divine command 'Read' carries the same weight as physical jihad in the path of Allah. The repetition of 'shahidan' highlights the multifaceted nature of this reward, covering death, resurrection, and eternal life.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. And from the previous chain from al-Hassan from Ali b. Muskan from Sulayman b. Khalid from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

If someone recites Surah Alaq in the day or night and then he dies the same day or night it is as though he achieved the rank of martyrdom and he would remain alive like a martyr who might have used his sword along with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.s.).
